el-greco-laocoon.webp.scene: Laocoön and his sons struggle with the serpents on the ground, a nude among them, and behind lies not Troy but El Greco's Toledo, with the wooden horse walking toward its gate. The two figures at the right may be gods watching.

rubens-the-fall-of-phaeton.webp.subject: phaeton
rubens-the-fall-of-phaeton.webp.scene: Struck by Jupiter's thunderbolt, Phaeton tumbles from the chariot as the horses rear in panic; the winged figures are the Hours, the seasons, scattered by the disaster.

titian-venus-and-adonis.webp.subject: venus-and-adonis
titian-venus-and-adonis.webp.scene: Adonis pulls away with his hounds, eager to hunt, as Venus clings to him; Cupid sleeps under a tree.

rembrandt-van-rijn-philemon-and-baucis.w.subject: philemon-and-baucis
rembrandt-van-rijn-philemon-and-baucis.w.scene: By lamplight in the humble cottage, Jupiter, at the head of the table, reveals himself, and the old couple understand who their guests are.

turner-the-rape-of-proserpine.webp.subject: proserpina
turner-the-rape-of-proserpine.webp.scene: Turner sets the abduction small in a vast golden landscape of Sicily; Proserpina's companions scatter in alarm as Pluto seizes her.

rossetti-proserpine.webp.subject: proserpina
rossetti-proserpine.webp.scene: Proserpina, queen of the underworld, holds the pomegranate she has bitten, which binds her there, while a shaft of daylight falls on the wall behind her. Jane Morris sat for her. Rossetti wrote the sonnet on the frame, in Italian and English.

leighton-the-return-of-persephone.webp.subject: proserpina
leighton-the-return-of-persephone.webp.scene: An oil sketch: Mercury lifts Persephone up out of the underworld to her mother Ceres, who stretches out her arms.

caravaggio-narcissus.webp.subject: narcissus
caravaggio-narcissus.webp.scene: Narcissus kneels over the dark pool, joined in a circle with his reflection. The attribution to Caravaggio is generally accepted but has been doubted.

waterhouse-echo-and-narcissus.webp.subject: narcissus
waterhouse-echo-and-narcissus.webp.scene: Narcissus lies gazing into the stream, blind to Echo, who sits watching him from the bank.

caravaggio-medusa.webp.subject: medusa
caravaggio-medusa.webp.scene: Painted on a round wooden parade shield for Cardinal del Monte to give to the Grand Duke of Tuscany: Medusa's head screaming at the instant of beheading, blood spurting. The face is said to be Caravaggio's own.

leighton-perseus-and-andromeda.webp.subject: perseus-and-andromeda
leighton-perseus-and-andromeda.webp.scene: Perseus swoops down on Pegasus, radiant against the sky, and shoots the dragon, which spreads its wings over the pale Andromeda.

rome-perseus-and-andromeda.webp.subject: perseus-and-andromeda
rome-perseus-and-andromeda.webp.scene: A wall painting from the villa of Agrippa Postumus at Boscotrecase, near Pompeii: Andromeda chained to the rock, the monster in the sea, and Perseus, on the right, taking her father's hand.

de-morgan-cadmus-and-harmonia.webp.subject: cadmus-and-harmonia
de-morgan-cadmus-and-harmonia.webp.scene: Harmonia stands naked on a rocky shore, gazing down at the serpent that was Cadmus as it coils round her.

leighton-orpheus-and-eurydice.webp.subject: orpheus-and-eurydice
leighton-orpheus-and-eurydice.webp.scene: Orpheus pushes Eurydice away and shields his eyes, as she clings to him, begging him to look. Browning wrote his poem for the painting, and its lines were printed with it.

waterhouse-circe-offering-the-cup-to-uly.subject: circe
waterhouse-circe-offering-the-cup-to-uly.scene: Circe holds out the drugged cup and her wand; in the mirror behind her throne we see Ulysses approaching, and one of his men turned into a pig lies at her feet.

waterhouse-circe-invidiosa.webp.subject: circe
waterhouse-circe-invidiosa.webp.scene: Circe, in a dress of peacock green, pours poison from a bowl into the sea where Scylla bathes, the water turning green around her.

waterhouse-ulysses-and-the-sirens.webp.subject: sirens
waterhouse-ulysses-and-the-sirens.webp.scene: Ulysses is bound to the mast as the Sirens, birds with women's heads, swoop round the ship; the oarsmen row with their ears stopped.

waterhouse-hylas-and-the-nymphs.webp.subject: hylas
waterhouse-hylas-and-the-nymphs.webp.scene: Hylas leans down with his jug to the lily pool, where seven pale nymphs rise out of the water and one takes him by the arm.

waterhouse-jason-and-medea.webp.subject: medea
waterhouse-jason-and-medea.webp.scene: Medea pours the potion into a vial at a table as Jason, behind her, waits.

waterhouse-psyche-opening-the-golden-box.subject: psyche
waterhouse-psyche-opening-the-golden-box.scene: Psyche kneels by a stream and lifts the lid of the box, and a vapour rises from it.

leighton-the-bath-of-psyche.webp.subject: psyche
leighton-the-bath-of-psyche.webp.scene: Psyche stands at the edge of a bath, lifting her robe, about to bathe; no single moment of the tale is shown.

de-morgan-helen-of-troy.webp.subject: helen
de-morgan-helen-of-troy.webp.scene: Helen stands in a rose garden holding a mirror, with Troy's sea behind; doves, the birds of Venus, at her feet.

de-morgan-cassandra.webp.subject: cassandra
de-morgan-cassandra.webp.scene: Cassandra tears her red hair as Troy burns behind her, scattered with roses.

leighton-captive-andromache.webp.subject: andromache
leighton-captive-andromache.webp.scene: At a fountain in a Greek town, Andromache, in black, waits her turn with her pitcher among the chattering women, the captive Hector foresaw.

leighton-electra-at-the-tomb-of-agamemno.subject: electra
leighton-electra-at-the-tomb-of-agamemno.scene: Electra, in black, stands at her father's tomb with her hands raised to her head in grief.

de-morgan-night-and-sleep.webp.subject: night-and-sleep
de-morgan-night-and-sleep.webp.scene: Night and her son Sleep float over the land at dusk, she in dark robes, he scattering poppies, the flower of sleep.

leighton-the-garden-of-the-hesperides.we.subject: hesperides
leighton-the-garden-of-the-hesperides.we.scene: Three nymphs sit under the golden-apple tree, one entwined with the serpent, in a circular picture.

rome-three-graces.webp.subject: graces
rome-three-graces.webp.scene: A Roman marble copy of a Greek group of the second century BCE, in the classic pose: the outer two face us, the middle one is seen from behind.

rodin-aurora-and-tithonus.webp.subject: aurora-and-tithonus
rodin-aurora-and-tithonus.webp.scene: A marble in which the faces of the dawn goddess and her ageing mortal lover emerge from the rough stone.

renoir-diana.webp.subject: diana
renoir-diana.webp.scene: Renoir's first big Salon picture, a nude model posed as the huntress with a bow and a dead deer, so as to make a modern nude acceptable. The Salon rejected it.

edward-robert-hughes-dianas-maidens.webp.subject: diana
edward-robert-hughes-dianas-maidens.webp.scene: The goddess's nymphs at rest in the woods.

caravaggio-amor-vincit-omnia.webp.subject: cupid
caravaggio-amor-vincit-omnia.webp.scene: A grinning, naked Cupid tramples on the instruments of music, war, learning and power: love conquers all. Made for the collector Vincenzo Giustiniani, who is said to have kept it behind a curtain.

caravaggio-sleeping-cupid.webp.subject: cupid
caravaggio-sleeping-cupid.webp.scene: Painted in Malta: a sickly child Cupid sleeps on his bow and quiver, perhaps a figure of love put to rest.

titian-cupid-with-the-wheel-of-time.webp.subject: cupid
titian-cupid-with-the-wheel-of-time.webp.scene: A grisaille, painted in tones of grey: Cupid leans on a wheel, perhaps the wheel of time or fortune. Its purpose, perhaps a cover for a portrait, is unknown.

titian-venus-with-a-mirror.webp.subject: venus
titian-venus-with-a-mirror.webp.scene: Two cupids hold up a mirror and offer a crown as Venus covers herself with a fur-lined cloak. Titian kept this picture in his house until his death.

burne-jones-the-mirror-of-venus.webp.subject: venus
burne-jones-the-mirror-of-venus.webp.scene: Venus shows a group of girls their faces in a still pool; they kneel, absorbed in their reflections.

crane-the-mirror-of-venus.webp.subject: venus
crane-the-mirror-of-venus.webp.scene: Walter Crane's design of the same theme, women gazing at their reflections.

burne-jones-the-garden-of-pan.webp.subject: pan
burne-jones-the-garden-of-pan.webp.scene: Pan sits piping by a stream in a deep valley, playing to a man and woman beside him.

burne-jones-the-feast-of-peleus.webp.subject: feast-of-peleus
burne-jones-the-feast-of-peleus.webp.scene: The gods feast at a long table in the open air as Discord arrives with the golden apple.

burne-jones-the-tree-of-forgiveness.webp.subject: phyllis-and-demophoon
burne-jones-the-tree-of-forgiveness.webp.scene: The moment of Demophoön's return: Phyllis springs out of the flowering almond tree and wraps her arms round her faithless lover, who tries to pull away.

de-morgan-the-dryad.webp.subject: dryads
de-morgan-the-dryad.webp.scene: A dryad stands half within the trunk of her tree, her feet rooted in it.

de-morgan-flora.webp.subject: dryads
de-morgan-flora.webp.scene: Flora, goddess of spring, scatters blossoms before a loquat tree. Painted in Florence in May 1894; on a scroll at her feet, in Italian, she says that she comes from Florence and is Flora, and will now make her home among Scottish mountains, a nod to the patron who bought it, the Scottish-born shipowner William Imrie.

leighton-crenaia-the-nymph-of-the-dargle.subject: dryads
leighton-crenaia-the-nymph-of-the-dargle.scene: Leighton imagined a Greek nymph for the Dargle, a river in County Wicklow, Ireland.

degas-alexander-and-bucephalus.webp.subject: alexander
degas-alexander-and-bucephalus.webp.scene: An early history painting by Degas, never finished: the young Alexander strokes the horse as his father and the court look on.

burne-jones-the-wheel-of-fortune.webp.subject: fortune
burne-jones-the-wheel-of-fortune.webp.scene: Fortune, tall and grave, turns her great wheel, on which a slave, a king and a poet, all naked, are bound, one rising as another falls.

leighton-the-fisherman-and-the-syren.web.subject: fisherman-and-syren
leighton-the-fisherman-and-the-syren.web.scene: The mermaid rises out of the sea and wraps herself round the fisherman, drawing him down.

waterhouse-consulting-the-oracle.webp.subject: oracles
waterhouse-consulting-the-oracle.webp.scene: In a dark temple a priestess lies before a lamp and a mummified head, interpreting its words to a circle of women.

waterhouse-the-magic-circle.webp.subject: sorceresses
waterhouse-the-magic-circle.webp.scene: A sorceress draws a circle of fire on the ground with her wand, ravens and a toad at the edge, a cauldron smoking.

de-morgan-the-love-potion.webp.subject: sorceresses
de-morgan-the-love-potion.webp.scene: A sorceress in gold robes, her black cat at her feet, prepares a love potion among her books of magic.

leighton-daphnephoria.webp.subject: daphnephoria
leighton-daphnephoria.webp.scene: The procession of youths and girls carrying the laurel pole up to the temple of Apollo at Thebes.

greece-volute-krater.webp.subject: amazons
greece-volute-krater.webp.scene: An Athenian bowl for mixing wine with water, painted with a battle between Greeks and Amazons.

egypt-nefertari-led-by-isis.webp.subject: egypt-afterlife
egypt-nefertari-led-by-isis.webp.scene: A copy made for the Met of a painting in the tomb of Nefertari, the great wife of Ramesses II: the goddess Isis takes the queen by the hand to lead her into the afterlife.

egypt-book-of-the-dead-of-nauny.webp.subject: egypt-afterlife
egypt-book-of-the-dead-of-nauny.webp.scene: A papyrus of spells buried with Nauny, a royal daughter and chantress: she stands before the gods as her heart is weighed.
egypt-book-of-the-dead-of-nauny.webp.uncertain: The scene described is the usual one in this papyrus; check against the Met's description.

near-east-bahram-gur-and-azadeh.webp.subject: bahram-gur
near-east-bahram-gur-and-azadeh.webp.scene: A Sasanian silver plate: Bahram Gur on his camel shoots at the gazelles, Azadeh behind him with her harp.

millais-ophelia.webp.subject: ophelia
millais-ophelia.webp.scene: Millais shows Ophelia after her fall, floating on her back and singing, in the moments before she sinks. He painted the riverbank on the Hogsmill in Surrey over five months of 1851, every flower exact and many chosen for their meaning, and then painted Elizabeth Siddal lying in a bath of water in his London studio; the lamps warming it went out and she caught a severe cold.

waterhouse-ophelia.webp.subject: ophelia
waterhouse-ophelia.webp.scene: Waterhouse shows the moment before the fall: Ophelia sits on the willow bough over the water, flowers in her lap and in her hair, absorbed in herself.

manet-the-tragic-actor.webp.subject: hamlet
manet-the-tragic-actor.webp.scene: Manet's portrait of the actor Philibert Rouvière in the role of Hamlet, dressed in black, against an empty background. Rouvière died while the picture was being painted.

brown-cordelia-parting-from-her-sisters..subject: cordelia
brown-cordelia-parting-from-her-sisters..scene: Cordelia, about to leave with the King of France, turns from her sisters with her hand raised, as they look back at her coldly.

hunt-claudio-and-isabella.webp.subject: measure-for-measure
hunt-claudio-and-isabella.webp.scene: In his prison cell, Claudio, his hand on the chain round his leg, pleads with his sister Isabella, in a novice's habit, who puts her hands on his heart and refuses. Through the window is the sunlit world outside.

leighton-the-feigned-death-of-juliet.web.subject: juliet
leighton-the-feigned-death-of-juliet.web.scene: Juliet lies as if dead on her bed in her wedding dress, and her family, Paris and Friar Laurence gather in the room, the friar alone knowing the truth.

hughes-the-long-engagement.webp.subject: orlando
hughes-the-long-engagement.webp.scene: Hughes began this picture as Orlando in the Forest of Arden, and then painted out his Shakespearean lovers and put in a modern couple: a poor curate and his fiancée, kept from marrying for years until he can afford it. The woman's name, Amy, is carved on the tree trunk, half overgrown with ivy.

edward-robert-hughes-orlando.webp.subject: orlando
edward-robert-hughes-orlando.webp.scene: A young figure in a cap with long red-gold hair, in a wood.
edward-robert-hughes-orlando.webp.uncertain: The title Orlando suggests As You Like It, but the figure may be Rosalind disguised as the youth Ganymede, or Orlando himself; no catalogue entry was found to settle it.

millais-mariana.webp.subject: mariana
millais-mariana.webp.scene: Mariana stands at her embroidery to stretch her back, by a stained-glass window, in autumn; dead leaves fall on the table and a mouse runs across the floor. Millais exhibited it with lines from Tennyson.

stillman-mariana.webp.subject: mariana
stillman-mariana.webp.scene: Mariana rests her chin on her hand by a window of bottle-glass roundels, waiting.
stillman-mariana.webp.uncertain: The picture is taken to be Mariana of the moated grange; it is not certain whether Stillman meant Shakespeare's or Tennyson's.

waterhouse-mariana-in-the-south.webp.subject: mariana
waterhouse-mariana-in-the-south.webp.scene: Mariana kneels before a shrine of the Virgin, her own face reflected in the mirror before her, with letters scattered on the floor.

hunt-the-lady-of-shalott.webp.subject: lady-of-shalott
hunt-the-lady-of-shalott.webp.scene: The moment the curse falls: the Lady stands caught in the threads of her unravelling tapestry, her hair flying, while Lancelot rides past in the round mirror behind her. Hunt worked on it for many years; it was finished with the help of Edward Robert Hughes when his eyesight failed.

waterhouse-the-lady-of-shalott.webp.subject: lady-of-shalott
waterhouse-the-lady-of-shalott.webp.scene: The Lady sets out for Camelot in her boat, the tapestry she wove trailing in the water, three candles before her, two already blown out.

waterhouse-i-am-half-sick-of-shadows-sai.subject: lady-of-shalott
waterhouse-i-am-half-sick-of-shadows-sai.scene: Waterhouse's last version, painted in 1915: the Lady stretches back from her loom, weary of the reflected world, as two young lovers appear in the mirror.

burne-jones-king-cophetua-and-the-beggar.subject: cophetua
burne-jones-king-cophetua-and-the-beggar.scene: The beggar maid sits barefoot and still on a high throne, holding anemones, while the king, his crown in his hands, sits below her looking up.

hughes-april-love.webp.subject: millers-daughter
hughes-april-love.webp.scene: A young woman stands in a summer house, turned away in tears from a quarrel; her lover, hardly seen in the shadow, bows his head over her hand. Rose petals lie on the floor.

waterhouse-the-soul-of-the-rose.webp.subject: maud
waterhouse-the-soul-of-the-rose.webp.scene: A woman in a garden presses her face to a rose on the wall, breathing in its scent. Also called My Sweet Rose.

waterhouse-a-mermaid.webp.subject: mermaid
waterhouse-a-mermaid.webp.scene: A mermaid sits on the shore combing her long hair, a shell of pearls beside her.

burne-jones-the-beguiling-of-merlin.webp.subject: arthur
burne-jones-the-beguiling-of-merlin.webp.scene: The enchantress, Nimue, reads from Merlin's own book of spells as he sinks helpless into a flowering hawthorn. Burne-Jones based it on the medieval French Romance of Merlin, in which Merlin is imprisoned in a hawthorn bush. The model for Nimue was Maria Zambaco, with whom he had a love affair.

burne-jones-the-last-sleep-of-arthur-in-.subject: arthur
burne-jones-the-last-sleep-of-arthur-in-.scene: Arthur sleeps on a bier in Avalon, watched over by queens and attendant women. Burne-Jones worked on the huge canvas for seventeen years and left it unfinished at his death in 1898.

brown-the-death-of-sir-tristram.webp.subject: arthur
brown-the-death-of-sir-tristram.webp.scene: Tristram sings to Isolde with his harp as King Mark leans over from behind with his sword.

hughes-la-belle-dame-sans-merci.webp.subject: belle-dame
hughes-la-belle-dame-sans-merci.webp.scene: The knight walks his horse through a wood, leading it by the bridle, with the lady sitting sideways on it; she leans down toward him, singing.

waterhouse-la-belle-dame-sans-merci.webp.subject: belle-dame
waterhouse-la-belle-dame-sans-merci.webp.scene: The lady kneels in the grass and draws the knight down to her with a strand of her long hair wound about his neck.

millais-isabella.webp.subject: isabella
millais-isabella.webp.scene: Millais's first Pre-Raphaelite picture: the family at dinner, where Lorenzo offers Isabella a blood orange, and her brother, kicking out at the dog, watches them with suspicion. Rossetti and other friends sat for the diners.

hunt-isabella-and-the-pot-of-basil.webp.subject: isabella
hunt-isabella-and-the-pot-of-basil.webp.scene: Isabella embraces the majolica pot that holds Lorenzo's head, tending the basil.

waterhouse-lamia.webp.subject: lamia
waterhouse-lamia.webp.scene: Lamia, a snakeskin over her arm, kneels before a knight who bends to her, in the woods.

brown-manfred-on-the-jungfrau.webp.subject: manfred
brown-manfred-on-the-jungfrau.webp.scene: The moment the chamois hunter seizes Manfred at the cliff edge.

brown-the-finding-of-don-juan-by-haidee..subject: don-juan
brown-the-finding-of-don-juan-by-haidee..scene: Haidée and her maid Zoe find Juan lying unconscious on the shore at the mouth of a cave.

millais-the-black-brunswicker.webp.subject: black-brunswicker
millais-the-black-brunswicker.webp.scene: A young officer of the Brunswickers, in his black uniform, is leaving for the battle; the woman he loves holds the door shut to keep him. On the wall is a print of David's Napoleon Crossing the Alps. The model for the woman was Kate Dickens, Charles Dickens's daughter.

rossetti-a-sea-spell.webp.subject: rossetti-poems
rossetti-a-sea-spell.webp.scene: A siren sits under an apple tree playing a stringed instrument, while a sea-bird stoops to her. Rossetti wrote the sonnet eight years before he painted the picture.

subject: fiammetta
rossetti-poems
rossetti-a-vision-of-fiammetta.webp.scene: Fiammetta stands among apple blossom shaking down petals, a red bird of death or love in the branches and a pale angel circling her head. Marie Spartali Stillman, herself a painter, sat for it.

rossetti-found.webp.subject: rossetti-poems
rossetti-found.webp.scene: Rossetti's only scene of modern life, worked on for thirty years and never finished. A young drover bringing a calf to market in London at dawn finds the country girl he once loved, now a prostitute, and she turns her face to the wall.

rossetti-the-day-dream.webp.subject: rossetti-poems
rossetti-the-day-dream.webp.scene: Jane Morris sits in the branches of a sycamore with a book on her lap, a sprig of honeysuckle forgotten in her hand.

rossetti-lady-lilith.webp.subject: lilith
rossetti-lady-lilith.webp.scene: Lilith sits combing her golden hair and gazing at herself in a hand mirror, surrounded by roses and poppies. Rossetti repainted the face in 1872–73, changing the model from Fanny Cornforth to Alexa Wilding.

rossetti-beata-beatrix.webp.subject: beatrice
rossetti-beata-beatrix.webp.scene: Rossetti's memorial to his wife, Elizabeth Siddal, who died of an overdose of laudanum in 1862: Beatrice in a trance at the moment of death, as a red bird, the messenger of death, drops a white poppy into her hands. Dante and the figure of Love look on from the street behind. On the frame is Dante's Latin quotation from Lamentations and the date of Beatrice's death, 9 June 1290.

rossetti-the-salutation-of-beatrice.webp.subject: beatrice
rossetti-the-salutation-of-beatrice.webp.scene: Beatrice walks toward us in the street, while Dante, in the background, is comforted by the winged figure of Love. The sonnet below is painted on the gilded frame Rossetti designed, in Italian and in his English. Jane Morris sat for Beatrice.

stillman-beatrice.webp.subject: beatrice
stillman-beatrice.webp.scene: Beatrice in a red dress, in the "subdued and goodly crimson" Dante describes.

rossetti-monna-vanna.webp.subject: beatrice
rossetti-monna-vanna.webp.scene: A sumptuous half-length of Alexa Wilding in a white and gold dress. Rossetti first called it Venus Veneta; the title Monna Vanna, "Lady Joan", comes from the Vita Nuova, where Vanna is Guido Cavalcanti's beloved, who walks before Beatrice.

botticelli-portrait-of-dante.webp.subject: dante
botticelli-portrait-of-dante.webp.scene: Dante in profile, in a red cap and hood with a laurel wreath.

rodin-the-kiss.webp.subject: francesca
rodin-the-kiss.webp.scene: Paolo and Francesca at the moment of their first kiss, the book still in Paolo's hand. Rodin made it for the Gates of Hell but found it too happy for them and made it a separate work.

rodin-the-thinker.webp.subject: gates-of-hell
rodin-the-thinker.webp.scene: First called The Poet: Dante sitting above the gates, thinking of the poem he is making and the souls below him.

rodin-la-douleur.webp.subject: gates-of-hell
rodin-la-douleur.webp.scene: A kneeling figure in grief, from among the damned of the Gates of Hell.
rodin-la-douleur.webp.uncertain: Its link to the Gates is from Rodin's working method; check the museum's note.

rossetti-la-pia-de-tolomei.webp.subject: pia
rossetti-la-pia-de-tolomei.webp.scene: Pia leans on the parapet of her husband's fortress in the Maremma, turning her wedding ring, letters and a rosary beside her, rooks in the sky and fever mist on the marsh below.

stillman-mia-suora-rachel.webp.subject: leah-and-rachel
stillman-mia-suora-rachel.webp.scene: Rachel sits gazing into her hand mirror.

stillman-fiammetta-singing.webp.subject: fiammetta
stillman-fiammetta-singing.webp.scene: Fiammetta sings among musicians, from Boccaccio's sonnet "Of Fiammetta Singing", which Rossetti translated.
stillman-fiammetta-singing.webp.uncertain: The scene is described from the title; check against the picture.

stillman-the-last-sight-of-fiammetta.web.subject: fiammetta
stillman-the-last-sight-of-fiammetta.web.scene: From Boccaccio's sonnet, translated by Rossetti, in which the poet sees Fiammetta for the last time, borne up to heaven.
stillman-the-last-sight-of-fiammetta.web.uncertain: Rossetti's translation of Boccaccio's sonnet was not found in a public-domain text to quote.

stillman-the-first-meeting-of-petrarch-a.subject: petrarch-laura
stillman-the-first-meeting-of-petrarch-a.scene: Petrarch sees Laura at the door of the church in Avignon on Good Friday.

waterhouse-a-tale-from-the-decameron.web.subject: decameron
waterhouse-a-tale-from-the-decameron.web.scene: A young man with a lute tells a story to a circle of young women sitting on the grass in a walled garden.

botticelli-the-story-of-nastagio-degli-o.subject: nastagio
botticelli-the-story-of-nastagio-degli-o.scene: In the pine wood, Nastagio, who has wandered away from his friends, sees the naked woman fleeing the knight and his hounds and tries to beat off the dogs with a branch.

botticelli-the-story-of-nastagio-degli-o.subject: nastagio
botticelli-the-story-of-nastagio-degli-o.scene: The knight cuts out the woman's heart and throws it to the dogs, and in the background the chase begins again.

botticelli-the-story-of-nastagio-degli-o.subject: nastagio
botticelli-the-story-of-nastagio-degli-o.scene: The banquet in the pine wood, where the hunt bursts in among the guests and the women rise in horror. The panels were made for the wedding of Giannozzo Pucci and Lucrezia Bini in 1483, arranged by Lorenzo de' Medici, and carry the coats of arms of the families.

leighton-cymon-and-iphigenia.webp.subject: cymon
leighton-cymon-and-iphigenia.webp.scene: Cymon, leaning on his staff, stands transfixed at the sight of Iphigenia asleep under the trees with her maids, in the light of evening.

stillman-the-enchanted-garden-of-messer-.subject: ansaldo
stillman-the-enchanted-garden-of-messer-.scene: Dianora and her ladies walk through the magic garden blooming in the middle of winter, the snowy town outside its walls.

rossetti-bocca-baciata.webp.subject: bocca-baciata
rossetti-bocca-baciata.webp.scene: Fanny Cornforth, with a marigold in her hair and an apple on the ledge before her. Rossetti's first painting of a single woman in close-up, the type of all his later pictures.

rossetti-fair-rosamund.webp.subject: rosamund
rossetti-fair-rosamund.webp.scene: Rosamund leans from the window of her bower waiting for the king, the red thread that leads through the maze hanging beside her.

hughes-fair-rosamund.webp.subject: rosamund
hughes-fair-rosamund.webp.scene: Rosamund sits in her hidden garden with her lute and embroidery, while in the background Queen Eleanor has just found the way in. Poisonous foxgloves line the queen's path.

waterhouse-gather-ye-rosebuds-while-ye-m.subject: gather-rosebuds
waterhouse-gather-ye-rosebuds-while-ye-m.scene: Two young women gather roses in a garden.

burne-jones-love-among-the-ruins.webp.subject: love-among-ruins
burne-jones-love-among-the-ruins.webp.scene: Two lovers sit among ruined arches overgrown with briar roses, he anxious, she resting against him.

edward-robert-hughes-night-with-her-trai.subject: night-with-stars
edward-robert-hughes-night-with-her-trai.scene: Night sweeps through the dark sky with a sleeping child in her arms and a crowd of child-stars streaming behind her.

burne-jones-sidonia-von-bork.webp.subject: sidonia
burne-jones-sidonia-von-bork.webp.scene: Sidonia in her gold-netted hair and her black and white dress patterned like a web, plotting, with a figure glimpsed in the room behind. Burne-Jones painted her and her innocent cousin Clara as a pair in 1860.

marvellous-tree.webp.subject: segur-mouse
marvellous-tree.webp.scene: Rosalie, having torn the cloth, stands dazzled before the tree of jewels.

bonne-biche.webp.subject: segur-blondine
bonne-biche.webp.scene: Blondine, grown up and learned, throws her arms round the neck of the white doe, while Beau-Minon the cat watches.

tortoise.webp.subject: segur-blondine
tortoise.webp.scene: Blondine rides on the Tortoise's back through the dark forest on her six months' journey.

giant.webp.subject: segur-henry
giant.webp.scene: The giant looks over the crumbling wall at little Henry.

plant-of-life.webp.subject: segur-henry
plant-of-life.webp.scene: At the top of the mountain the little Doctor, in his black cloak with his book, greets Henry in the fairies' garden.

rosette.webp.subject: segur-rosette
rosette.webp.scene: Rosette and Prince Charmant walk in the palace garden in the evening, her diamonds shining.

night-in-the-forest.webp.subject: segur-ourson
night-in-the-forest.webp.scene: Violette sleeps on the moss under Ourson's coat while he sits watching over her.

crane-goody-two-shoes-picture-book.webp.subject: goody-two-shoes
crane-goody-two-shoes-picture-book.webp.scene: Walter Crane's design for the cover or a page of his Goody Two Shoes picture book.

botticelli-the-story-of-lucretia.webp.subject: lucretia
botticelli-the-story-of-lucretia.webp.scene: Three scenes in a Roman square: on the left Tarquinius threatens Lucretia, on the right she collapses as she dies, and at the centre her body lies on a bier while Brutus calls the soldiers to revolt.

rembrandt-van-rijn-lucretia.webp.subject: lucretia
rembrandt-van-rijn-lucretia.webp.scene: Lucretia stands with the dagger in her raised hand, her face full of sorrow, at the moment before she strikes.

gentileschi-lucretia.webp.subject: lucretia
gentileschi-lucretia.webp.scene: Lucretia, half dressed, grasps her breast and the dagger, looking upward, deciding.

botticelli-the-story-of-virginia.webp.subject: virginia
botticelli-the-story-of-virginia.webp.scene: Several scenes set in a single classical piazza: Virginia is seized, pleads before Appius, and is killed by her father, who then rides off to rouse the army.

bellini-an-episode-from-the-life-of-publ.subject: scipio
bellini-an-episode-from-the-life-of-publ.scene: A long, low painted frieze in imitation of a marble relief: Scipio restores the captive to her betrothed, and the gold is brought.

rubens-decius-mus-addressing-the-legions.subject: decius-mus
rubens-decius-mus-addressing-the-legions.scene: A design for the first of the tapestries: Decius, on a platform, tells his troops of his dream.

rubens-agrippina-and-germanicus.webp.subject: agrippina
rubens-agrippina-and-germanicus.webp.scene: The two heads in profile, Agrippina in front, as on a Roman cameo.

waterhouse-the-favourites-of-the-emperor.subject: honorius
waterhouse-the-favourites-of-the-emperor.scene: The young emperor feeds his doves and pigeons on the rug while his ministers, bowing, wait to be heard.

rodin-a-burgher-of-calais.webp.subject: burghers-of-calais
rodin-a-burgher-of-calais.webp.scene: Jean d'Aire, one of the six, standing with the key of the town in his hands and the rope round his neck.

rodin-jean-daire.webp.subject: burghers-of-calais
rodin-jean-daire.webp.scene: Another cast of Jean d'Aire, the burgher who carries the keys.

millais-the-princes-in-the-tower.webp.subject: princes-in-the-tower
millais-the-princes-in-the-tower.webp.scene: The two boys stand together at the foot of a dark stair in the Tower, the younger clinging to his brother, listening to the footsteps they fear.

millais-the-order-of-release-1746.webp.subject: order-of-release
millais-the-order-of-release-1746.webp.scene: The wife hands the order to the jailer, her husband, his arm in a sling, falls on her shoulder, and she holds their sleeping child. Effie Gray, who later married Millais, sat for her.

millais-the-north-west-passage.webp.subject: north-west-passage
millais-the-north-west-passage.webp.scene: An old captain sits clenching his fist at a table of charts while his daughter reads to him from a log; the model was the adventurer and writer Edward Trelawny, friend of Byron and Shelley.

hunt-a-converted-british-family-shelteri.subject: converted-family
hunt-a-converted-british-family-shelteri.scene: Inside a hut a family tends the wounded missionary, while outside a druid crowd hunts another.

brown-the-last-of-england.webp.subject: last-of-england
brown-the-last-of-england.webp.scene: The couple sit huddled under an umbrella at the stern of the ship, she holding the hand of the baby hidden under her shawl, the cliffs of Dover behind.

hunt-the-miracle-of-the-holy-fire.webp.subject: holy-fire
hunt-the-miracle-of-the-holy-fire.webp.scene: The packed Church of the Holy Sepulchre at the moment the fire appears, filled with pilgrims, priests and soldiers.

hunt-london-bridge-on-the-night-of-the-m.subject: royal-wedding-1863
hunt-london-bridge-on-the-night-of-the-m.scene: The crowd on London Bridge on the night of the wedding, lit by illuminations; Hunt put himself and his friends into it.

hunt-may-morning-on-magdalen-tower.webp.subject: may-morning
hunt-may-morning-on-magdalen-tower.webp.scene: The choir and fellows on the top of the tower at sunrise, singing the hymn.

leighton-cimabues-celebrated-madonna.web.subject: cimabue
leighton-cimabues-celebrated-madonna.web.scene: Leighton's first great success, bought by Queen Victoria in 1855: the procession through Florence, Cimabue walking beside his picture leading the boy Giotto, and Dante watching at the right.
